tagline: Following Lee's army from the Potomac fords to Antietam Creek.
intro: The byway starts at White's Ferry on the Potomac, near where Confederate soldiers forded into Maryland in September 1862, and follows the campaign north through Poolesville and Barnesville, over Sugarloaf Mountain, which served troops as a lookout, past the Monocacy battlefield to Frederick, then west across South Mountain to Boonsboro and Sharpsburg.

On September 17 the armies met along Antietam Creek, and by dusk the Union held the field. On September 22 Lincoln issued the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation. It did not free the people enslaved in Maryland, a state not in rebellion. That took a new state constitution in 1864.

moments.title: Poolesville
moments.text: Union troops gathered here in 1861 before crossing for Ball's Bluff, and in 1863 Confederate horsemen came storming through on their way to Gettysburg.

moments.title: Washington Monument State Park
moments.text: Boonsboro's citizens marched up on July 4, 1827, and raised the first completed monument to George Washington, a dry-laid stone tower near the crest of South Mountain.

moments.title: Tolson's Chapel
moments.text: Built of logs in 1866 by Sharpsburg's Black residents on land given by a free Black man, the chapel was a schoolhouse too, and blackboards remain on its side walls.
